newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed sharply higher after a surprise fall in U.S. employment figures sparked a rally, particularly in longer-dated guilder paper.
News that U.S. September non-farm payrolls fell 40,000 when they had been expected to rise 166,000 forced traders who had sold ahead of the figures to scramble to buy.
"People are really hurting," said one trader, referring to the short squeeze which sent long bonds up by 30-50 ticks.
Ten-year bonds had been under selling pressure this week because of a perception they were overvalued following a rally which sent yields down to the lowest levels since January.
But the yield discount to Germany continued to narrow because bunds were seen as better value.
"Guilders were underperforming tremendously. They're too expensive to buy," said another trader, attributing this to an excess of sellers over buyers in the 2005/2006 maturities.
He said investors may switch back into guilders from bunds when the 10-year spread reached seven or eight basis points, from the current 10 basis points.
A dealer attributed the German bond market's outperformance to its greater liquidity. "We often see that in a squeeze. People move into bunds first," he said.
But he said the Dutch market's rally would be short-lived, with prices likely to weaken on Monday as investors shied away from moving along the steepening yield curve.
"You pick up extra yield but you take more risk," he said.
